questions.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem With a Negative Sine
questions.worked_solution:
For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=16$ and $\phi =\frac{\theta }{2}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})]}^{16} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(16\cdot \frac{\theta }{2})-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(16\cdot \frac{\theta }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem to Fractions
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡5\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡5\theta ]^{3}}=[\operatorname{cos}⁡5\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡5\theta ]^{-3}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-3$ and $\phi =5\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡5\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡5\theta ]^{3}} & =[\operatorname{cos}⁡5\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡5\theta ]^{-3} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(5(-3)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5(-3)\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-15\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-15\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(15\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(15\theta ).
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem With a Negative Sine
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )]}^{5}} & =4{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )]}^{-5}.\end{aligned}
$$

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-5$ and $\phi =4\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )]}^{-5} & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-5\cdot 4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-5\cdot 4\theta )] \\  & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-20\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-20\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-20\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-20\theta )] & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\theta )-[-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\theta )]] \\  & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
4{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )]}^{-5}=4[\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\theta )].
$$
